subject: genetics
question: **Type:** application A PCR reaction is run with template DNA, two primers, deoxynucleotides, and Taq polymerase. During which step of the PCR cycle is the temperature lowered so that the primers can base-pair with the template?

options.text: Denaturation, in which the temperature is raised to about 95 degrees C to separate the strands
Extension, in which the temperature is raised to about 72 degrees C so that DNA polymerase adds nucleotides
Annealing, in which the temperature is lowered to about 55 degrees C so that the primers base-pair with the template
Ligation, in which the temperature is held at about 37 degrees C so that DNA ligase seals the strands

explanation: PCR cycles three temperatures: denaturation near 95 degrees C separates the strands, annealing at about 55 degrees C lets the primers base-pair with their complementary template sequences, and extension near 72 degrees C lets Taq polymerase synthesize new strands. A describes denaturation, which melts the duplex rather than binding primers. B describes the extension step, and D invokes ligation, which is used in cloning rather than in PCR, because amplification relies on polymerase and not ligase.
